subject.title: Session modelOverride persists across gateway restarts, silently overrides config default

question: Should `/new`/`/reset` or config-default changes automatically clear explicit and legacy `modelOverride` pins, or should explicit pins remain strict with a separate bulk reset/reconcile tool?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve user and legacy pins while clearing auto fallback pins, so changing the behavior affects persisted user state and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Preserve pins, add explicit reset tooling
options.body: Keep explicit session pins strict by default, and add a visible bulk reset or reconcile path with dry-run/reporting for users who want config defaults to take over.

options.title: Clear explicit pins on reset
options.body: Make `/new` and `/reset` always inherit the configured primary, accepting that existing users who rely on persistent per-session model pins will see behavior change.

options.title: Make config outrank pins after restart
options.body: Treat config-default changes as higher precedence than stored session pins after a gateway restart, which maximizes surprise-free defaults but weakens per-session pin semantics.

recommendation.title: Preserve pins, add explicit reset tooling
recommendation.body: Keep explicit session pins strict by default, and add a visible bulk reset or reconcile path with dry-run/reporting for users who want config defaults to take over.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is product/documentation policy for model-selection semantics, and steipete authored the current docs that state the active contract.
